issues.legal_issue: Delegating to the executive the power to extend enactments to a territory without its own legislature does not amount to an unconstitutional abdication of legislative power when the delegation is guided and confined to selecting suitable laws enacted by competent legislatures.
material_facts: The territory had no local legislature, and Parliament had legislative responsibility for it.
The challenged provision empowered the executive to extend to the territory enactments in force in a State, subject to restrictions or modifications.
The territory was small and situated among areas with their own legislatures, while Parliament had limited time to address its detailed legislative needs.
The executive’s role was to select suitable enacted laws for the territory, rather than to make a new law or change an enactment’s substance.
issues.conclusion: The delegation was valid and did not constitute abdication or effacement of Parliament’s legislative power.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 246(4) of the Constitution and section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, Parliament may delegate subordinate legislative tasks but must retain the essential legislative function of laying down policy and standards. The Court applied the policy-and-guidelines approach and the reasoning in In re Delhi Laws Act, [1951] SCR 747, and referred to Registrar of Cooperative Societies v. Kunhambu, [1980] 2 SCR 260, and Gwalior Rayon Silk Mfg. (Wvg.) Co. Ltd. v. Assistant Commissioner of Sales Tax, [1974] 2 SCR 879. A broad indication of policy is sufficient in this context; the delegation is not abdication where the executive selects among laws already enacted by competent legislatures for their suitability to local conditions.

rule.if: challenge_to_executive_extension_power and territory_without_local_legislature and executive_selects_enacted_laws and selection_guided_by_local_suitability and executive_cannot_make_substantive_law_changes

predicates.challenge_to_executive_extension_power: A proceeding challenges the validity of giving the executive authority to extend laws to a territory.
predicates.territory_without_local_legislature: The territory for which the laws are to be extended has no local legislature.
predicates.executive_selects_enacted_laws: The executive is empowered to select laws that have already been enacted by competent legislatures.
predicates.selection_guided_by_local_suitability: The executive selects laws by assessing their suitability to the territory’s local conditions.
predicates.executive_cannot_make_substantive_law_ch: The executive’s authority does not permit it to make a new law or substantially alter the substance of an enacted law.

issues.definition: When an extension-power challenge concerns a territory without a local legislature and the executive’s guided role is limited to selecting enacted laws without substantive changes, the delegation is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A valid power to extend existing enactments to a territory may include authority to extend later enactments or amendments to those laws.
material_facts: The executive had authority to extend existing laws to a territory without its own legislature.
Parliament’s limited time to consider the territory’s legislative needs also made it difficult to consider later amendments to laws selected for extension.
The challenged extension concerned an amendment enacted after the original law.
issues.conclusion: Authority to extend future enactments or amendments is a necessary corollary of a valid power to extend existing laws.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied In re Delhi Laws Act, [1951] SCR 747, and reasoned that if the executive may extend an existing law because Parliament lacks time to consider it, the executive may also extend later amendments to that law for the same reason. The delegated power remains subject to the policy and limits that make the original extension power valid.

predicates.challenge_to_future_law_extension: A proceeding challenges the executive’s authority to extend a law enacted after the original grant of extension authority.
predicates.valid_power_to_extend_existing_laws: The executive has a valid authority to extend existing laws to the territory.
predicates.later_law_amends_or_supplements_an_exten: The later enactment amends or supplements a law that has been extended to the territory.
predicates.extension_serves_the_same_local_legislat: Extending the later enactment addresses the same need to provide suitable laws for the territory without requiring Parliament to consider every legislative detail.

issues.definition: When a valid power to extend existing laws is challenged as to later enactments that amend or supplement those laws for the same local need, the later extension is permissible.

issues.legal_issue: An enactment may be extended to a territory even where related legislation already applies there, provided the new provisions do not repeal, conflict with, or become repugnant to the existing law.
material_facts: An existing parliamentary enactment governed rent matters in the territory.
The later enactment sought to be extended added provisions addressing aspects not covered by the existing enactment.
The added provisions were not inconsistent with the existing enactment and did not displace it.
The challenge argued that extension was impermissible because legislation on the broader subject already applied in the territory.
issues.conclusion: The existence of related legislation did not bar extension of provisions that supplemented it without conflict or repeal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 permits extension of an enactment that adds to existing law so long as it does not expressly or impliedly repeal, conflict with, or become repugnant to that law. The Court applied a constructive interpretation of the provision and relied on Hari Shankar Bagla v. State of Madhya Pradesh, [1955] 1 SCR 380, and Lachmi Narain v. Union of India, [1976] 2 SCR 795.

rule.if: challenge_to_extension_into_territory_with_existing_law and existing_law_applies_to_related_subject and extended_law_adds_uncovered_provisions and no_repeal_conflict_or_repugnance

predicates.challenge_to_extension_into_territory_wi: A proceeding challenges an extension of an enactment to a territory where related legislation already applies.
predicates.existing_law_applies_to_related_subject: A law already applicable in the territory addresses the same broad subject as the enactment proposed for extension.
predicates.extended_law_adds_uncovered_provisions: The enactment proposed for extension adds provisions addressing matters not covered by the existing law.
predicates.no_repeal_conflict_or_repugnance: The added provisions neither expressly or impliedly repeal nor conflict with or become repugnant to the existing law.

issues.definition: Where an extension adds uncovered provisions to existing related law without repeal, conflict, or repugnance, the supplementary extension is valid.

issues.legal_issue: Restrictions and modifications made when extending an enactment are permissible only when they are incidental or ancillary and do not substantially deviate from the enactment.
material_facts: The executive’s notification extended an enactment subject to specified modifications.
The modifications in the notification were very minor.
The extended enactment otherwise applied in its existing form.
issues.conclusion: The modifications were within the permissible scope of the extension power because they were minor and did not substantially deviate from the enactment.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, restrictions and modifications accompanying an extension may be only incidental, ancillary, or subservient changes and may not substantially alter the enactment. The Court relied on Lachmi Narain v. Union of India, [1976] 2 SCR 795.

predicates.challenge_to_modifications_in_extension_: A proceeding challenges changes made by the executive while extending an enactment to a territory.
predicates.notification_makes_modifications: The extension notification alters or limits some aspect of the enactment being extended.
predicates.modifications_are_incidental_or_ancillar: The changes are limited to incidental, ancillary, or subservient adjustments.
predicates.no_substantial_deviation_from_extended_l: The changes do not substantially depart from the enactment’s substance or scheme.

issues.definition: When an extension notification makes only incidental or ancillary changes without substantially departing from the enactment, those changes are valid.

issues.legal_issue: An executive notification extending rent-law amendments to a territory is valid when the amendments supplement the rent law already applicable there without conflict and the notification makes only minor modifications.
material_facts: A parliamentary enactment had extended the principal rent law to the territory.
The State legislature later amended that rent law, and the executive issued a notification extending those amendments to the territory.
The amendments added provisions concerning aspects not covered by the parliamentary enactment and were not inconsistent with it.
The notification extended the amendments with only very minor modifications.
The appeals and petitions challenged the notification’s validity.
issues.conclusion: The notification was valid; the appeals and writ petitions were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 permits extension of an enactment in force in a State, including later amendments, where the additions do not repeal or conflict with existing law. Any modifications in the notification must remain incidental and must not substantially deviate from the extended enactment. The Court relied on In re Delhi Laws Act, [1951] SCR 747, Lachmi Narain v. Union of India, [1976] 2 SCR 795, and Hari Shankar Bagla v. State of Madhya Pradesh, [1955] 1 SCR 380.

rule.if: challenge_to_rent_law_extension_notification and existing_rent_law_applies_in_territory and amendments_add_uncovered_matters and no_conflict_with_existing_rent_law and notification_changes_are_minor

predicates.challenge_to_rent_law_extension_notifica: A proceeding challenges an executive notification extending rent-law amendments to a territory.
predicates.existing_rent_law_applies_in_territory: A rent law is already applicable in the territory.
predicates.amendments_add_uncovered_matters: The amendments add provisions concerning matters not addressed by the rent law already applicable in the territory.
predicates.no_conflict_with_existing_rent_law: The amendments do not repeal, conflict with, or become repugnant to the existing rent law.
predicates.notification_changes_are_minor: The notification’s modifications to the enactment being extended are only minor.

issues.definition: When a challenged rent-law extension adds uncovered matters without conflicting with existing rent law and makes only minor changes, the extension notification is valid.
